body.statement: The proposed equal-alphabet certified class and \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\) are incomparable in the ambient mixed-type latent-structure universe. On \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(q)}(K,J)\), every selected observed variable has support \(q\), so Chen et al.'s discrete sufficient-measurement requirement \( |\operatorname{supp}(X_j)|>|\operatorname{supp}(H_k)|\) fails when both supports equal \(q\); the dense ternary witness is therefore outside their two-sufficient-measurement class. Conversely, \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\) permits continuous measurements and graphs without two disjoint triangular views, so it is not contained in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(q)}(K,J)\). Completeness in Chen et al. supplies a discretization with full-rank tables, whereas this project derives full rank from the finite local certificate without assuming completeness or larger-support measurements.
body.justification: The class relation prevents the new certificate from being presented as a disguised instance of completeness or two sufficient measurements.
body.gap: Chen et al. (2025, Proposition 4.2, Definition D.3, and Theorem 4.19) cover mixed-type measurements through completeness and two sufficient measurements, not equal-state double-triangular tables.
body.consumer: It tells practitioners whether a mixed-type tensor-rank guarantee or the local categorical certificate applies to a given item bank.
body.proof_tex:
The source lemma records the two-sufficient-measurement requirement of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\). In the present certified class, positive support and positive measurement tables imply
\[
 |\operatorname{supp}(H_k)|=q
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 |\operatorname{supp}(X_j)|=q
\]
for every \(k,j\). All measurements are discrete. Hence no observed variable in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(q)}(K,J)\) is a sufficient measurement in the cited sense, because the required strict inequality \(q>q\) is false. Thus the two-sufficient-measurement condition fails for every member of the certified class.

This class is nonempty. On the graph \(\Gamma^{\star}\), the calculations in the proof attached to Proposition~\textnormal{prop:ternary-witness} establish strict positivity, measurement nondegeneracy, the graph conditions, and \(\Delta_{\mathrm{DT}}>0\) at \(P^{\star}\). These are finitely many strict polynomial or rational inequalities and persist in a relative neighborhood. Lemma~\textnormal{lem:positive-faithful-parameters-dense} supplies a faithful positive Markov parameter in that neighborhood. It is therefore a member of \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(3)}(3,8)\), but the equal-support calculation puts it outside \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\). Hence \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(q)}(K,J)\) is not contained in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{Chen}}\) in the ambient universe in which both classes are compared.

Conversely, the cited definition expressly permits continuous sufficient measurements. For example, take one nondegenerate finite latent variable and three conditionally independent location-family continuous children with distinct latent-indexed locations and everywhere positive noise densities. The shifted densities are linearly independent, so the finite-state conditional expectation operator is complete; generic positive choices are faithful. This is a mixed-type member allowed by the cited class, but it cannot belong to \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cert}}^{(q)}(K,J)\), whose observed coordinates all have the finite state space \(\mathcal Q\). Thus the reverse containment fails already by support type. Independently, the multifactor graphs permitted by the cited class need not be double triangular: if two latent coordinates have only jointly parented observed children, then every such row contains both coordinates, so whichever coordinate is placed first in an order violates the required zero for the later coordinate. Finally, the cited discretization result explains the different rank mechanisms: completeness yields a discretization with a full-rank conditional table, whereas the present Theorems~\textnormal{thm:local-factorization} and~\textnormal{thm:certificate-frontier} derive full rank from the finite local determinants. This proves all asserted comparisons.
